title: Zero-section purity in affine space
statement:
Work in the finite-coefficient setting of [def-pur-conventions], with $\Lambda=A=A_{E,n}$ for any $n\geq1$. Let $B$ be a separated finite-type $k$-scheme [def-weil-finite-type-morphism, def-weil-proper-morphism], let $c\geq0$, and let $p_c:\mathbf A^c_B\to B$ and $z:B\hookrightarrow\mathbf A^c_B$ be the projection and zero section of [def-sbc-affine-space]. Use the specified Tate twists [def-coefficient-twists-detailed] and exceptional inverse image [def-weil-exceptional-inverse-image].

For every coordinate divisor $D_i=\{t_i=0\}$ use the supported Cartier-Kummer class of [lem-amb-cartier-kummer-map]: form the ordinary etale Kummer boundary with $\mu_{\ell^a}\otimes_{\mathbf Z/\ell^a}A$ for any $a\geq1$ such that $\ell^aA=0$, then realize it on the specified pro-etale Tate twist. This prescription is independent of $a$ and is the normalized affine-line orientation of [thm-pur-affine-line-orientation] on the domain of its affine-line datum; it specifies that same boundary at every $n\geq1$. Products mean the supported cup product of [def-pur-supported-cup], transported by the exact monoidal site comparison. The $c$-fold product, or unit for $c=0$, gives a canonical isomorphism
$$
\mathrm{th}_c:A_B\xrightarrow{\sim}Rz^!A_{\mathbf A^c_B}(c)[2c],
$$
compatible with every base change $B'\to B$ between separated finite-type $k$-schemes. Under this isomorphism $1$ is the class $\partial\kappa(t_1)\cup\cdots\cup\partial\kappa(t_c)$; equivalently $Rz^!A_{\mathbf A^c_B}\cong A_B(-c)[-2c]$.

Let $\gamma_{p_c,A_B}$ be the ordered affine-space comparison of [def-pur-affine-space-comparison], using the all-finite-level integration-transposed affine-line maps of [def-pur-affine-line-purity-comparison]. Then $\mathrm{th}_c$ is the inverse of
$$
Rz^!A_{\mathbf A^c_B}(c)[2c]\xrightarrow{Rz^!(\gamma_{p_c,A_B})}Rz^!Rp_c^!A_B\xrightarrow{\sim}A_B,
$$
where the last map is the adjunction-preserving composition identification for $p_cz=\operatorname{id}_B$. Equivalently, the integration map transposed from $\gamma_{p_c,A_B}$ sends the class of the zero section to $1$.

proof.text: Use the coordinate tower $X_r=\mathbf A^r_B$, $q_r,s_r$ and $W_r=A_{X_r}(r)[2r]$. The normalized line-adjunction lemma checks the geometry and all finite coefficient levels, and identifies each actual $\gamma_{q_r,-}$ as a natural isomorphism. The twisted section-normalization lemma gives the invertible maps $u_r:W_r\to Rs_r^!W_{r+1}$ and their identity evaluation under $Rs_r^!\gamma_{q_r,W_r}$. These use exactly the prescribed Cartier-Kummer maps and Tate lines, without a condition on the ramification index.

Let $C_c$ be the specified ordered supported coordinate product and $\theta_c$ its adjunct. The product-recursion lemma gives $\theta_0=1$ and $\theta_{r+1}=d_r^{-1}Rz_r^!(u_r)\theta_r$. Induction makes every $\theta_c$ invertible, since the $u_r$ of the preceding step and the composition comparisons are invertible. The same lemma identifies its adjoint with the ordered coordinate product, including the empty product. Thus $\mathrm{th}_c=\theta_c$ has precisely the stated generator.

Apply the tower-normalization induction with these $u_r$ and the ordered comparisons: its hypotheses are the natural line isomorphisms and twisted identities from Step 1. It gives $b_c\theta_c=1$ and $b_c=\theta_c^{-1}$, where $b_c$ is $Rz_c^!\gamma_{p_c,A_B}$ followed by composition for $p_cz_c=1$. Its transpose formula says that the integration adjoint to $\gamma_{p_c,A_B}$ sends $C_c$ to $1$. This proves the requested agreement with the actual ordered affine-space comparison.

The product-recursion lemma supplies compatibility of $\theta_c$ with the specified closed exceptional base-change mate for every $B'\to B$, including nonflat maps, and independence of the annihilating exponent. Finally the closed immersion twist isomorphism moves the invertible Tate factor through $Rz_c^!$; tensoring $\theta_c$ with $A_B(-c)[-2c]$ gives $Rz_c^!A_{X_c}\cong A_B(-c)[-2c]$. At $c=0$ every formula is the identity. In Lean, substitute the structure-map equality, unfold classBaseChange to the same named coordinateSourcePullback used by the product identity, and apply the first clause of coordinate_section_product_baseChange.

blueprint_update.statement:
In the purity conventions of this chapter ([def-pur-conventions] fixed setting),
$A=A_{E,n}$, let $B$ be a
separated finite-type
$k$-scheme and let $z:B\hookrightarrow\mathbf A^c_B$ be the zero
section of the affine space of [def-sbc-affine-space]. The
$c$-fold exterior product of the normalized affine-line orientation of
[thm-pur-affine-line-orientation] is a canonical, base-change
compatible isomorphism

$$
\Lambda_B\xrightarrow{\ \sim\ }Rz^!\Lambda_{\mathbf A^c_B}(c)[2c],
$$

i.e. $Rz^!\Lambda\cong\Lambda_B(-c)[-2c]$; the product of the Kummer
boundaries of the coordinates $t_1,\dots,t_c$ corresponds to $1$.
Moreover this isomorphism is $(-1)^c$ times the inverse of the composite
$Rz^!\Lambda_{\mathbf A^c_B}(c)[2c]\xrightarrow{Rz^!(\gamma_{p_c,\Lambda_B})}
Rz^!Rp_c^!\Lambda_B\cong\Lambda_B$, where $\gamma_{p_c,\Lambda_B}$ is the
affine-space purity comparison of [def-pur-affine-space-comparison]
(an isomorphism by [cor-pur-affine-space-purity]) and the last
identification is the composition law for $p_cz=\operatorname{id}_B$:
the affine-space purity comparison, restricted along the zero section,
carries the product of the Kummer boundaries of the coordinates to
$(-1)^c$. Equivalently, the integration map transposed from
$\gamma_{p_c,\Lambda_B}$ sends the class of the zero section,
$\partial\kappa(t_1)\cup\cdots\cup\partial\kappa(t_c)$, to $(-1)^c$, and
it sends the product $c_{D_1}\cup\cdots\cup c_{D_c}$ of the Cartier
classes of [lem-amb-cartier-kummer-map] of the coordinate hyperplanes
$D_i=V(t_i)$ to $1$. The sign is that of [lem-pur-divisor-class](b):
$\partial\kappa(t_i)=-c_{D_i}$, and the projective-line trace of
[def-amb-p1-trace] is normalized by $t_q(c_1(\mathcal O(1)))=1$.

proof.text:
First work on the ordinary etale site. The explicit adjunction of
[cor-amb-affine-space-adjunction] gives
$p_c^\times\Lambda_B=\Lambda_{\mathbf A^c_B}(c)[2c]$.
Composition of adjunctions, as in
[def-weil-exceptional-inverse-image], and
$p_cz=\operatorname{id}_B$ therefore identify
$Rz^!\Lambda_{\mathbf A^c_B}(c)[2c]$ with $\Lambda_B$.
In rank one this identification sends a class supported on the zero
section $s(Y)\subset\mathbf A^1_Y$ to its integral: its image in
$H^2(\mathbf P^1_Y,\Lambda(1))$ under extension by zero, followed by the
trace $t_q$ of [def-amb-p1-trace]. The Cartier map $c_{s(Y)}$ of
[lem-amb-cartier-kummer-map] for the divisor $s(Y)$ of $\mathbf P^1_Y$ is
supported on $s(Y)\subset\mathbf A^1_Y$ and forgets support to
$c_1(\mathcal O_{\mathbf P^1_Y}(s(Y)))=c_1(\mathcal O(1))=h$, so it
integrates to $t_q(h)=1$. By [lem-pur-divisor-class](b) the orientation
class of [thm-pur-affine-line-orientation] is
$\partial\kappa(t)=-c_{s(Y)}$, so it integrates to $-1$. Iterating the
affine-line adjunctions, the section class
$\partial\kappa(t_1)\cup\cdots\cup\partial\kappa(t_c)$ is the ordered
exterior product of the rank-one classes, and by the projection formula
its integral is the product of the rank-one integrals, namely $(-1)^c$;
likewise $c_{D_1}\cup\cdots\cup c_{D_c}$ integrates to $1$. Since
$(-1)^c$ is a unit, the $c$-fold product of the orientations is an
isomorphism, equal to $(-1)^c$ times the inverse of the identification
obtained from the adjunction.
The even shifts and twists add by [def-coefficient-twists-detailed].
The comparison [thm-sf-ambient-adjoint-class] transports the
composition and counits to the stated finite etale-origin objects.
Finally the rank-one orientations commute with base change by
[prop-pur-affine-line-orientation-base-change], and all the Cartier maps
and the explicit affine-space counits commute with base change, by
[lem-amb-cartier-kummer-map], [prop-asd-smooth-base-change].
Hence the resulting zero-section isomorphism has the claimed
normalization and base-change compatibility. No general relative
Kunneth assertion with closed support is needed for this calculation.
Finally, $\gamma_{p_c,\Lambda_B}$ is the transpose of the composite
affine-line adjunction ([thm-pur-affine-line-purity] identifies each
affine-line comparison with the adjoint of the normalized trace, and
[def-pur-affine-space-comparison] composes them along the tower), so
the identification $Rz^!\Lambda_{\mathbf A^c_B}(c)[2c]\cong\Lambda_B$
obtained above from $p_c^\times\Lambda_B=\Lambda_{\mathbf A^c_B}(c)[2c]$
and $p_cz=\operatorname{id}_B$ is exactly $Rz^!(\gamma_{p_c,\Lambda_B})$
followed by the composition isomorphism; with the sign $(-1)^c$ computed
above this is the stated compatibility with the affine-space purity
comparison.
